title: Record the MR !7 review fixes and their verification
message:
Record the MR !7 review fixes and their verification

The S2 progress in the vessel study now lists the four review findings
and their commits, the Vailand re-route the corrected schedule check
forced, the gate helper's grace wait, the review-round gate, soak, and
CI results, and how S3 continues: stacked on the reviewed S2 head at
vessels-s3-base while MR !7 is open. VESSEL_BENCHMARKS.md records the
repeated ferry soak.

title: Give timed crew reports a grace wait in the login helper
message:
Give timed crew reports a grace wait in the login helper

The movement check waits a fixed 33 seconds for the 30-second cast-off
report and 14 for the 13-second weigh-anchor report. The S2 pass caught
the cast-off report at the very end of its window, and a review-round
run missed it by a moment and failed. wait_for_game_output() now waits
ten seconds more, once, when the report has not arrived; a server on
time costs nothing extra.

title: Route the Vailand passage clear of the coast
message:
Route the Vailand passage clear of the coast

With room edges crossed in the order the track meets them, three legs of
the Vailand Iron Passage ran through land the old diagonal step had
skipped, and the corrected schedule check rejected the route: the
southwest leg clipped the beach at (-508,215), the final approach to the
central port clipped the beach corner at (-468,204), and the northwest
leg from the central offing turned into the spit at (-501,192). The
southwest turn moves to (-513,215), the central offing to (-504,191),
and the harbor offing to (-467,193), so the last leg runs due north up
open water into the port. setschedule on a copy of the loop, from the
north port, now accepts it. The campaign gate starts the merchant at the
new offing, heading north; the passage is 368 rooms.

title: Validate scheduled routes along the line the hull will sail
message:
Validate scheduled routes along the line the hull will sail

The schedule preflight stepped one rounded room at a time toward each
waypoint with no speed or heading, but the live autopilot carries both
through a turn: a frigate arriving eastbound at a buoy at speed 17 and
steering north for the next waypoint runs on into the room past the
buoy before she comes round. When that room was land, setschedule
accepted the route and the scheduled run paused there.

scheduled_route_is_traversable() now sails a copy of the hull over the
route. The helm physics move into vessel_sail_tick(), shared by the
live tick and the preflight; the autopilot's heading order and speed
cap (autopilot_order_heading()) and its climb (autopilot_climb_toward())
are shared the same way; and rooms are checked with vessel_chart_cell(),
which allocates nothing. The copy sails at the hull's present maximum
speed with rigging and rudder whole, holds through waits, stops at the
end of a one-way route, and runs a loop on to its second waypoint so
the turn after the closing leg is checked. The room-step helper
vessel_autopilot_next_position() had no other caller and is removed
with its test. A sharp-turn test finds the preflight entering exactly
the rooms the live autopilot enters, and refusing the route when the
room past the buoy is land.

title: Cross room edges in the order the hull's track meets them
message:
Cross room edges in the order the hull's track meets them

vessel_cross_room_edges() stepped diagonally whenever a tick carried the
hull past both edges of its room, as DurisMUD does. On an off-axis
course that skips a room: from (0.49, 0.49) on heading 60 at speed 30
the track crosses the east edge, then the north edge, yet only the
northeast room was entered, so a hull could pass through the corner of
a land room without it being checked. Each edge's crossing time (its
overshoot over the tick's travel across it) now orders the steps, and
only a crossing through the corner itself enters the diagonal room. A
refused room leaves the hull where its track met the edge.

title: Reach autopilot waypoints within their own room
message:
Reach autopilot waypoints within their own room

setwaypoint and waypoint_add() stored a five-room arrival radius, and
check_waypoint_arrival() fell back to it. With momentum sailing, a
one-way route to a player's port completed five rooms out and set its
speed order to zero, so the hull stopped short and never berthed; a
wait waypoint started its wait offshore. New waypoints now store
AUTOPILOT_ARRIVAL_TOLERANCE (0.5, the waypoint's own room), the value
the S2 content routes already use, and legacy migration 2026092901
moves existing rows at the old 5.0 default to 0.5. A test sails a
created route to a port and finds the hull berthed there.

title: Load a restored hull's owner before reconciling its berth
message:
Load a restored hull's owner before reconciling its berth

At boot, load_all_ship_interiors() reconciled the berth before loading
the owner. A player-owned hull saved at rest in port with no berth (for
example just after a cast-off) still had an empty owner, so
vessel_berth() treated it as public and made good its sail and rudder
for free. vessel_db_restore_berth() now loads the owner first, and a
database-backed test restarts a damaged owned hull in port.

title: Steady the vessel gates on a loaded host
message:
Steady the vessel gates on a loaded host

- The frontier and movement checks retry a setsail maneuver until the
  crew is ready instead of trusting a fixed six-second wait, which a
  busy server stretched past its ten vessel ticks.
- The hunter gate gives its target a tick to gather way before the
  forced encounter and reads the hull after it.
- The derelict gate snapshots Kohdee's saved objects with --skip-tz-utc:
  --compact drops the SET TIME_ZONE line, so the UTC timestamps it wrote
  came back shifted by the server's offset and the byte-exact restore
  check failed.

title: Leave water depth to the battle-stations crash check
message:
Leave water depth to the battle-stations crash check

The draft barrier closed every seaport to ship-class hulls: the Central
Vailand Sea Port and its approach lie on water one unit deep, and the
campaign merchant stopped a room short of the port. Depth no longer
refuses a room; S4 brings grounding back with the battle-stations crash
check, as 3.3.2 describes for land. The old setsail grounding goes too.

Crossing rooms now follows DurisMUD: the hull enters the room its
position lies in, diagonally when it crosses both edges in one tick,
matching the eight-direction grid that routes are validated on. The
hunter gate no longer requires a berth where its dock is not a port.

title: Accept fleet slots 10 through 19 in the hunter gate
message:
Accept fleet slots 10 through 19 in the hunter gate

Its slot checks matched ^[2-9][0-9]*$, which rejected slots 10-19 and
100-199; a development fleet of a dozen hulls hands the target slot 14.

title: Let reglist and pathlist parse their own arguments again
message:
Let reglist and pathlist parse their own arguments again

The list command validates a zone or two VNUM bounds before dispatching,
so since 500019db1 "reglist type 5" failed with "Both VNUM bounds must
be unsigned 32-bit integers" and "pathlist 50" looked for zone 50. Both
commands take a distance or a type, so they now skip that parsing. The
vessel frontier provisioner depends on the documented form.

title: Validate route rooms as a hull will find them
message:
Validate route rooms as a hull will find them

Scheduled-route validation read the generated map's sector even where a
static room sits on the map, so the harbor's east dock, a seaport built
over shallow water, failed the new draft check and every harbor and
campaign schedule was disabled at its next departure. Validation now
takes a static room's sector first, as the hull's position update does.

title: Make good an unowned hull's rigging when it berths
message:
Make good an unowned hull's rigging when it berths

Sail and rudder now limit speed and turning, so the wear and weather
that public and NPC hulls have always accumulated leaves them crawling:
every such hull in the development database had worn to 1 of 20. They
have no owner to repair them, so the harbor restores their sail and
rudder whenever they berth. The campaign fixture reset restores its
merchant the same way before it is placed on the route.

The development world has no west dock room at (-66, 92); the east dock
(room 1000390) is the harbor port that exists.

title: Move the vessel live gates to momentum sailing
message:
Move the vessel live gates to momentum sailing

Hulls launched in port now start berthed, speed is gathered over time,
and setsail is a one-room maneuver every five seconds, so the gates that
assumed instant speed and multi-room setsail jumps change with them:

- The builder check casts off before maneuvering; the frontier check
  maneuvers at rest, five seconds apart, and reads altitude and depth
  from the climb and dive replies; the regatta finishes by maneuver;
  the narrative check lets the warship gather way first.
- The harbor ferry runs at speed 10, the dock wait allows 300 seconds
  and the named-water crossing 150; the campaign windows watch the
  merchant's last leg into the central port; the hunter target casts
  off before the forced encounter; the soak waits for a paused ferry to
  come to rest before comparing positions.

A new --vessel-movement-check, run by test_vessel_movement_in_game.sh
through the shared harness, walks a boat through its berth, departure,
maneuvers, and re-berthing, and a warship through acceleration,
pacing, turning, all stop, and anchoring.

title: Come about in place and record where hulls come to rest
message:
Come about in place and record where hulls come to rest

The autopilot now holds its speed at zero while the bow is more than
90 degrees off the waypoint's bearing, so an out-and-back ferry turns at
the dock instead of swinging wide into the shore. A hull that comes to
rest saves its runtime row, which persists a new berth and the position
a paused autopilot holds. Route validation also checks the keel's
draft, matching the rooms a hull may enter.

title: Sail vessels on momentum at the Duris pacing
message:
Sail vessels on momentum at the Duris pacing

Study step S2 (decision D1). Orders now set targets that every 0.5 s
vessel tick converges on: speed moves by the class acceleration and
heading by the class turn rate, both scaled by the sailmaster tier, and
the turn also by speed and the rudder, so a smashed rudder no longer
answers the helm (L1). A hull covers speed / 90 rooms a tick along its
heading, crossing rooms one axis at a time so every room entered is
checked for terrain, depth, draft, and dock-fee clearance; a refused
room stops her at its edge (L3).

Maximum speed is the design speed times the sailmaster, load, and sail
factors and the terrain, weather, and altitude-lane percentage, plus
one with a seadog at the helm, so lost rigging stays lost until
repaired (L2). A hull at rest in port is berthed; undock casts off in
30 s or weighs anchor in 13, and the new anchor command holds a stopped
hull at sea. setsail becomes the harbor maneuver: one room at speed 6 or
less, every 5 s. The autopilot, hunters, merchants, and scheduled routes
all move through the same tick.

New src/vessels/vessels_movement.c holds the class handling table,
maximum speed, the movement tick, berths, departures, and maneuvers,
with production-linked tests in test_vessel_movement.c. Help changes in
both places; VESSEL_SYSTEM.md gains a Movement and Pacing section.
